items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: when Duke Ellington, I was taking Paul Gonsalves’ chair, because he had some gigs he was doing, so I did I guess about four or five performances in the Boston area.

ctx.x: Terrific. Oh, could we chat for a moment about your big band experience? Because I know you were with Hampton —

Oh yeah, Hampton and Duke Ellington and Count Basie. It was a wonderful experience for me because I got a chance to be around and to play with musicians who I had great admiration for. To be able to see the level on how they function, and what the important things were. And I remember, now when I first got with Count Basie, it was here up in the Westchester area. And we were playing, I forget the venue. But we had went into — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

prior to that time – into the store, you know, to buy some snacks or whatever we wanted before hit time, and I guess maybe we had an hour or so before we hit. And I just was, I kind of lost track of time, and I’m just looking for things. And I look up and nobody’s in the store, all the musicians are gone. Nobody said to me listen it’s time to hit. And I went to look at my watch and I’m running to get in, and when I get in the club everybody’s on the bandstand and Basie’s getting ready to hit. I had the stuff, and…
